title: Unify streaming backpressure + retry semantics across Python/TS/Go; migration guide & changelog automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood SDK v2 introduces two important, potentially breaking behaviour changes: (1) an explicit streaming flow-control/backpressure API ("stream sessions" and "flow tokens") to avoid unbounded client-side buffering; and (2) a converged retry model that clarifies idempotency and backoff across languages.

Problem statement:
Previously each SDK had slightly different streaming ergonomics (Python buffered all events until user iterated, TS emitted immediately, Go had ad-hoc channel semantics) and inconsistent retry defaults (different backoffs and idempotency header naming). This caused bugs in production for customers who ported integrations across languages and for server-side middlewares that rely on deterministic retry/ordering semantics.

Goal:
Ship language-consistent streaming and retry semantics, provide a clear migration guide for v1->v2, add concrete examples (Python/TypeScript/Go), and automate changelog entries for SDK releases so users can discover breaking changes and upgrade steps.

Deliverables:
- SDK runtime changes across Python/TS/Go to implement "stream sessions" and explicit flow-token API.
- RetryPolicyBuilder library shared design and per-language implementation.
- Migration guide doc (Confluence) with copyable code samples for common patterns (chat streaming, long-poll ingest, resumable streams).
- Examples repo updates (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples) with three runnable demos.
- Changelog automation job: detect exported API deprecations and generate templated changelog PRs on release branches.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Behavioral parity tests pass for canonical streaming scenarios (prefix-caching, mid-stream cancellation, client backpressure) across languages.
- Retry unit/integration tests validate idempotency header behavior and deterministic backoff for transient vs non-retriable errors.
- Migration guide published and linked from SDK repo README.
- Changelog automation opens draft PRs with detected deprecations and suggested migration snippets.

Non-goals:
- Changing server-side streaming protocol. This ticket focuses on SDK ergonomics and docs only.

Implementation notes and proposed API (summary):
1) Streaming: introduce StreamSession object that is created by the client call (e.g., client.start_stream(...)). The session exposes: request_flow_token() to request N tokens worth of work, pause()/resume() for client-controlled backpressure, and close(reason) for graceful termination. Sessions carry a stable session_id used in metrics and in-flight cancellation.

2) Retries: centralize policy via RetryPolicyBuilder with named presets (conservative, default, aggressive). Default policy in v2 is "default": jittered exponential backoff with cap 30s, max_attempts=4 for non-idempotent, and max_attempts=8 for idempotent requests. Idempotency is determined by explicit Idempotency-Key header or by operation semantics (see migration).

3) Migration flags: SDK v2 will expose a runtime flag `compat_v1_streaming=true/false` to help customers toggle legacy behaviour while they migrate. Flag will be temporary for one minor release.

Per-language migration notes (short):
- Python: replace generator-based streaming (for event in client.stream(...)) with `with client.open_stream(...) as s:`; call s.request_flow_token(5) inside loop. We will provide a small adapter `legacy_stream_adapter` that mimics v1 buffering for quick migration.

- TypeScript: current event emitter API will be preserved but augmented with `session.requestTokens(n)` and `session.pause()/resume()`. Example migration snippet added to README.

- Go: introduce StreamSession as a typed struct with channel helpers; provide `LegacyBufferingReader` to emulate old semantics.

Changelog automation design (summary):
- A CI job (`tools/sdk-changelog-detector`) will scan each language's public surface for symbols removed/renamed/marked deprecated between tags (v1.x -> v2.0). For each finding the job generates a markdown entry with: description, suggested migration snippet (pulled from a small library of templates keyed by symbol), risk level, and PR link if auto-fix applied. Draft PRs are opened against each SDK repo with `changelog/auto/v2-migrations` branch.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Adding flow-control primitives makes the API surface larger and slightly more complex for simple use cases. Mitigation: provide high-level helpers and `legacy_stream_adapter` for one-release compatibility.
- Automated changelog can produce noisy PRs; mitigation: require a human reviewer (SDK owner) and gate job to open only draft PRs.

Observability/telemetry changes:
- Add `stream.session_id` to SDK metrics and traces. Emit counters for `flow_token_requested` and `flow_token_consumed` per session. Document which telemetry keys are added so customers can update dashboards.

Docs & examples (concrete links to draft artifacts):
- Confluence migration doc (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/123456789/Streaming+and+Retry+Migration+v1->v2
- Example PR (TS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/412
- Python legacy adapter PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/678
- Changelog detector tool repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/sdk-changelog-detector

Notes for reviewers:
- Please validate the Python generator -> context-manager example for typical async and sync patterns.
- Evaluate the default retry presets for real customer workloads (conservative may be too cautious for platform internal integrations).
- Review the changelog templates for tone and clarity.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-language streaming parity: passes canonical scenarios test suite
Retry behavior: deterministic and documented for idempotent vs non-idempotent ops
Migration guide published and linked from SDK READMEs
Changelog automation opens draft PRs with templated migration snippets
plan: Week 1: finalise API design, implement shared RetryPolicyBuilder prototyping
Week 2: implement StreamSession in TypeScript + examples, update examples repo
Week 3: Python and Go implementations + legacy adapters, add telemetry keys
Week 4: write migration Confluence doc, add docs to SDK READMEs
Week 5: enable changelog-detector in CI, open draft PRs and iterate on reviewer feedback
